subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should the filesystem `read` tool add a generic binary-document fallback for Office/PDF files, or should document handling be left entirely to dedicated parser/provider/file-input surfaces?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent shape affects core tool semantics, existing PDF/document-extract surfaces, and whether OpenClaw adds only a safe default or parser-backed document handling in core.

options.title: Adopt a narrow read guard
options.body: Add a focused MIME/extension guard for known binary document formats that returns a helpful fallback and routes users to `pdf` or document-extraction tools without parsing documents in `read`.

options.title: Add parser-backed read support
options.body: Teach `read` to extract text for selected document formats, accepting the added security, dependency, and maintenance surface after explicit design review.

options.title: Defer to dedicated tools only
options.body: Leave `read` text/image-only and rely on tool descriptions plus PDF/document/file-input surfaces, accepting that the reported binary-read token waste may continue when the model chooses `read`.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow read guard
recommendation.body: Add a focused MIME/extension guard for known binary document formats that returns a helpful fallback and routes users to `pdf` or document-extraction tools without parsing documents in `read`.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent read-tool ownership and core/product-boundary history make this the best available routing candidate for the read semantics decision.
